text: Agent Horizon evaluates risk across an agent trajectory, not just one message or tool call. The key idea is simple: individually permitted actions can compose into an unsafe security or privacy outcome.

In the first scenario, the agent is allowed to read a product roadmap, a manufacturing reservation, and an executive calendar. Weather and cafeteria events are added as smokescreen noise. No single source reveals the final conclusion.

Horizon keeps the evidence that materially contributes to the active state and filters the noise. Correlating the three relevant sources creates new knowledge: Project Nova is likely launching in mid-to-late October. That fact did not exist in any one source.

This is a semantic delta. The derived conclusion is more sensitive than the individual observations. When the agent tries to publish it outside the enterprise trust boundary, Horizon blocks the action.
An isolated content check can see that every read was authorized. Horizon adds trajectory context: provenance, correlation, and the new state created by the agent.
The second scenario contains no sensitive content. The agent deploys a new version, shifts production traffic, and disables the old deployment while rollback is still available.

The last request deletes the final rollback artifact. The API call is authorized, but the consequence is not equivalent: production changes from reversible to effectively irreversible. Horizon detects this consequence delta and requires human approval.
Agent Horizon asks what becomes newly knowable or newly possible as the trajectory evolves. Security and privacy are properties of the evolving state, not just the individual event.
